messages:
marta: FYI seeing 95th->p99 latency jump in eu-west-1 rack-18 after the allocator rebalance sweep. gen endpoints +180ms. anyone else?
leo: yep, same. traces show an extra rack hop when redispatch happens, kv cache miss rate spikes right after allocation move.
anita: checked the TOR counters on tor12, tx queue spike + some CRC errors. could be NIC offload flapping or MTU mismatch after reconfigure.
ryan: curious — how much would carving a tiny dedicated micro-silo cost vs SLA hit? rough back-of-envelope pls.
leo: before we carve, could try soft-prefer-local routing: prefer same-rack for new allocs and delay cross-rack redispatch by 30s for warmups. cheap experiment.
marta: allocator version is dedicated-scheduler v2.3.4, job started rolling ~08:12 UTC (that matches the jump).
anita: dump from tor12 (excerpt):
```
May 05 08:13:12 tor12 kernel: eth0: tx_queue_len=1000 tx_errors=23 rx_errors=0
May 05 08:13:13 tor12 ethtool: tx-queue 3 offload toggled
```
leo: found allocator trace: `redispatch: tenant=cohort-x -> rack-18 -> rack-3` repeated ~300x in 15m. looks like churn.
sre-bot: alert: alloc-events: redispatch_count=312 since 08:10, p95_latency_up=true
ryan: quick cost calc (very rough): 4 gpus * $0.85/hr * 24 * 30 = $2448/mo. if we need 8 gpus to hit throughput -> ~$4896/mo.
marta: thanks. rough SLA penalty from repeated p99s last 24h already ~ $3.2k-equivalent (est). so dedicated could be cheaper if it stabilizes. need proper calc.
leo: proposal: 1) roll `prefer-local=true` flag for cohort-x for 1% traffic (canary) 2) if p95 improves by >30% promote to 10% then full until rebalancer fix 3) collect net/alloc traces.
anita: also opening ticket with network team to sanity-check tor12 port config, ask for capture during the canary window.
ryan: I'll run a detailed cost vs SLA model and post numbers by EOD.
marta: can someone kick off the canary? small safe rollout instructions: `internal-scheduler set-cohort-flag cohort-x prefer-local=true --rate 0.01` then watch `metrics.redispatch.rate` and `kvcache.hit_rate`.
leo: on it. will start canary at 09:00 UTC and watch for 20 minutes.
anita: tagging network: @netops please watch tor12 during 09:00-09:30 UTC for CRC/queue anomalies.
sre-bot: deploy-job: scheduler flag rollout started by leo at 09:00 UTC (canary 1%).
leo: initial 20m: redispatch_rate down ~65%, kvcache hit_rate +12%, p95 down ~45ms.
marta: nice. can we extend to 10% and monitor cost signal?
ryan: extending to 10% temporarily should not change monthly cost materially, will update model.
anita: tor12 still shows occasional tx errors but lower volume. opened ticket NET-7123 with pcap attached.
leo: next: if the prefer-local change holds, we should either: A) make permanent scheduler tweak B) change rebalancer to prefer warm buckets during decisioning C) carve dedicated micro-silo for top noisy tenants.
marta: agree. leaning B first (fix allocator logic) + fallback policy to stall redispatch until kvcache warm. that's lower cost than dedicated and preserves locality.
ryan: I'll prepare a one-pager cost/benefit for exec: include run rates, expected SLA savings, and worst-case dedicated expense.
leo: action items: leo -> continue 10% canary + run full trace; anita -> follow up NET-7123; ryan -> cost/exec note; marta -> open infra bug for rebalancer hysteresis.
marta: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
leo: :thumbsup:
ryan: will post numbers soon.
sre-bot: monitor note: p95 back to baseline for canary cohort at 10% after 40m.
